_comment: Session Ledger + Checkpoint wiring for .claude/settings.json.
Merge into your existing settings; do not replace the whole file. Paths are
relative to the project root. Every hook must be executable:
chmod +x .claude/hooks/*.sh
System in one line: auto-compaction is OFF, you fire the checkpoint skill by
hand ('prepare compact') before every /compact, and a PreCompact guardrail
blocks /compact until that checkpoint left a fresh marker. Nothing automatic.
TURNING AUTO-COMPACTION OFF: use env.DISABLE_AUTO_COMPACT, NOT a top-level
'autoCompactEnabled' key. That key does not exist in the settings schema and is
silently ignored (the schema sets additionalProperties:true, so it neither errors
nor does anything). The schema does document DISABLE_AUTO_COMPACT as an environment
setting, and the env block in settings.json is committable, so this is repo-wide and
reproducible. Related knobs the schema lists: DISABLE_COMPACT (disables compaction
entirely), CLAUDE_CODE_AUTO_COMPACT_WINDOW and CLAUDE_AUTOCOMPACT_PCT_OVERRIDE
(threshold tuning). Merge the env block key-by-key if your settings.json already
has one; do not replace an existing env object.
SessionStart hooks: 'startup' primes once and restores the ledger regardless of its
age (chats are timeless, and a clock that retires a ledger strands live conversations);
'compact'/'resume' hand the reasoning back. A running auto-compaction does not raise
SessionStart at all, which is one more reason auto is off here.
PreCompact matcher 'manual': the guardrail only guards manual /compact (auto is off).
It fails open on any error and lets an 'auto' trigger through, so it can never trap
you in a window you cannot compact. It blocks on a missing marker AND on a marker
sitting over an empty ledger, so a checkpoint that captured nothing does not pass.
UserPromptSubmit -> prompt-checkpoint.sh: asking for the checkpoint in words has to keep
working after a compaction. The skill description carries trigger phrases, but skill
descriptions are the one piece of startup content a compaction does not restore, so that
route dies at exactly the moment it is needed: 'prepare for compaction' is said before a
compaction, and by then there has usually already been one. A hook is configuration, not
context, so it survives. It only injects an instruction, it never blocks or edits the
prompt, and it ignores anything longer than 160 characters so a discussion ABOUT the
checkpoint does not fire one. Off switch: SESSION_LEDGER_PROMPT_TRIGGER=off.
Stop -> ledger-lint.sh: both mechanical guards live here, and neither is visible to
the user. (1) It warns when the ledger outgrows its budget or grows sections outside
the canonical seven; that exists because the prose instruction to keep the ledger small
was measured against a real session and lost (177 lines / 18 KB, 13 sections).
(2) OPT-IN, off by default: it can fire the checkpoint by itself once the transcript
has grown past SESSION_LEDGER_CHECKPOINT_TRIGGER_KB (400) since the last marker. That
is the one thing the PreCompact guardrail cannot do, because PreCompact output reaches
only the user and never the model. It ships off anyway: a pass that fires itself
interrupts work nobody asked to interrupt, and the guardrail already refuses an
unprepared /compact, so nothing is lost by waiting for the human to fire it.
Both are delivered as hookSpecificOutput.additionalContext with exit code 0, so they
reach the model as a system reminder and never appear in the transcript. Rate-limited,
so neither can nag every turn. Off switches: SESSION_LEDGER_LINT=off for the size
check. Opt into the self-firing pass with SESSION_LEDGER_CHECKPOINT_TRIGGER=on.
The SESSION_LEDGER_* env values above are what the hooks actually read: the manifest
documents intent, the shell hooks take env vars. Keep the two in sync.
SESSION_LEDGER_PROJECT_STATE names the second carrier, the one that outlives a task.
It defaults to .claude/project-state.md, and that default is only right for a project
that has no state file yet. Point it at the file you already keep, or the checkpoint
creates a SECOND state document next to your existing one and the two drift apart.
Measured in a real repository: an 83 KB curated status file was the actual source of
truth, nothing named it, and the kit was one checkpoint away from starting a rival.
Whatever the value ends up being, decide whether that file belongs in git: the ledger
and the checkpoint marker are session-local and gitignored, this one is not.
WHY MAX_CHARS IS 6000, and why it is a band and not a hard line: three numbers
describe the same thing, and the advertised one has to be the strictest, or green is
a false promise. The re-inject body gets 6550 characters, the prime restore gets 6000
(it also prints the maintenance protocol and shares one 10000-character hook cap;
measured worst case at 6000 is 8595, so ~1400 of headroom). The smallest restore is
therefore 6000, and that is what MAX_CHARS mirrors.
SESSION_LEDGER_TOLERANCE_PCT exists because of a measured failure mode: with a hard
5000 and a warning on the first character over, a real session started rewriting
entries and stripping markup to land at 4999. That is character golf against a
counter, it burns a turn and changes nothing about what the ledger carries. The
warning now fires only past MAX_CHARS + tolerance, and its text says explicitly to
delete finished content rather than to compress wording.
LOADING THE LEDGER BACK after a /compact (measured live, 2 runs):
- SessionStart(compact) reinject DOES fire on a manual /compact, but a few minutes
late, so it can lose the race against your next message. Best-effort, kept.
- A PostCompact hook was tried and REMOVED: it failed live with 'Hook cancelled'
and its injection is not doc-supported anyway. Do not re-add it.
- The reliable carrier is the ledger FILE on disk. When both hooks miss, the model
re-reads .claude/session-ledger.md itself and continues. Make that deterministic
by adding one line to your project's instruction file (CLAUDE.md/AGENTS.md), which
survives compaction. The restore output ends with a canary line, so the instruction
can key off it: 'After a compaction, if you do not see a Canary CTX-LEDGER-RESTORED
line in context, read .claude/session-ledger.md before continuing.'
